narrative:
The model predicts an 85% chance that you will leave your job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This high probability means the system sees strong signs that you are likely to depart soon, based on patterns from many similar employees.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this prediction were your overall years of experience, whether you have received other job offers, and how long you have been with this current organization. These stood out as the top drivers compared with everything else in your profile.

Your 6-10 years of total experience pushed the prediction toward leaving. While many employees predicted to stay have only 1-5 years, your mid-level experience matches people who often explore new opportunities. Similarly, having received other job offers strongly increased the likelihood of departure, as this is relatively uncommon among those expected to remain. Finally, your 1-5 years in your current role also contributed to the prediction of leaving, since a large share of employees who stay tend to have either very short or much longer tenures here.

Taken together, these signals suggest you may be at a natural career crossroads. The organization should discuss your career goals with you openly. You might consider what would make staying more attractive, such as clearer advancement paths or better rewards. Addressing these areas could change the outlook and support your growth here.
